body: The restructure's invariant is that the boot of a stand task or fixture, the act through a driver session and the read of the answer (refusal, diff, caused, snapshot text) move into shared helpers and keep doing what they do. The same stand checks hold this: the same test functions under the same names, the same assertions on the same readings, in the same layout modes.

A helper moves only setup and reading code, never the subject or bound of an assertion. No stand check is weakened, skipped or ignored, and expected roles, names, tab orders and other expectations stay stated once in their shared tables, never copied into a helper.

Every check stays one target per file. No test file is merged, split or renamed, no test target is added or removed, and the targets named by the stand-repeat leg (the stand checks repeated three rounds) are unchanged.

The shared helpers live under the blitz tests' shared modules (common, session_common, fixtures), which the checks include. P3 decides which module takes which helper, by what each family already includes.

A shared helper in a module that non-stand targets also include must not break those targets' build and must not add a dead-code warning under the clippy leg. It follows the module's existing convention for helpers unused in some targets.

The answer-read helpers must pass on the driver's answers exactly as the checks read them before: the driver refusal causes, the actions answer and its causes, the snapshot diff and its entries, and the parts and state tokens of the snapshot text form. They must not re-shape or re-parse any of these.
Nothing a check asserts on leaves the repo differently. A helper writes no id, name, value or typed text into a test name or an assertion message, because a driver refusal holds nothing of the call.
Test code only. Nothing changes in the engine, driver, harness, stand or product code, and no crate or dependency is added.

The snapshot and accessibility-tree readers that the helpers call stay behind the accessibility feature, just as they were when the checks called them directly. A helper reaching them compiles only where the checks that use it already enable that feature.

The duplication reading is taken before and after with the code audit's own tool (jscpd, Rust format, default minimum tokens, gitignore respected) over the audit's directories. It is summarized as the audit record does: the percentage to two places, duplicated and total lines, clones, the src / test / mixed split and the top ten.

The readings it moves against are 3.80 % → 3.81 % → 3.89 %, with test pairs 266 → 291 → 307 while src pairs held at 223. P4 settles which earlier reading counts as "back under", and whether that is read as the whole percentage or as the test split.

The moved setup still passes every CI gate it passed before: the accessibility test leg in the slow tier, the accessibility checks that gate CI and the stand checks repeated three rounds. Each check stays deterministic across the repeated rounds.

body_fields.convention: each shared helper that a stand check calls keeps expected roles, names and orders stated once in the shared expectation tables, not restated beside the helper
each stand check reached through a helper stays an accessibility assertion written as a Rust test over the AccessKit tree, inside the accessibility test leg
each stand check keeps its place in the three-round stand-repeat leg under its own named target

The rows that state how roles are mapped, how ARIA attributes are read and written, how accessible names take precedence and how hidden or inert content is excluded from the tree do not bind. No engine or tree-building code changes.

The rows on the platform accessibility adapter, the accesskit_xplat adapter, AccessKit event routing and the absence of an adapter on the stand binaries do not bind. The chunk adds no adapter and changes none.

The rows on the accessibility tier, on the accessibility feature being default-on or off in the browser, and on how accessibility reach is stated in the capability statement do not bind. The chunk changes no feature default or reach statement.

The rows on visual design do not bind: contrast thresholds, the contrast lint and its finding, scrollbar and select-list colours, the stand accent colour, zoom and colour scheme. No paint or contrast code changes.
The rows on cognitive accessibility, such as an invalid state not shown by colour or class alone, do not bind. No stand markup or styling changes.
The rows on password masking, password caret placement, IME enabling and option labels leaving only as pixels do not bind. The chunk changes no product behaviour behind these rules.
The rows on the UI graph state registration and the Dioxus document reached-handler record do not bind. These components are product code the chunk does not touch.

body: Restructure invariant. The repeated setup units move into shared helpers: booting a stand task or fixture, acting through a driver session, and reading an answer (refusal, diff, caused, snapshot text). Each stand check keeps the same test functions under the same names, the same assertions on the same readings, and the same layout modes. The existing stand checks hold this, run both directly and by the stand-repeat leg's named targets.

One target per file in blitz-tests (the 2026-10-10 decision stands). No test file is merged, split or renamed, and no test target entry is added or removed. The blitz-tests target pin and the stand-repeat leg's named targets stay unchanged.

The shared helpers live in non-target shared test modules in subdirectories of the blitz-tests tests directory. Stand-check helpers belong in non-target modules, and shared fixtures are stated once. Each check reaches a helper by including the module, not as a target of its own.

A helper moves only setup and reading code. It never moves the subject or the bound of an assertion. No test is weakened, skipped or marked ignored. Where a fixture's precondition is asserted first, it stays first in the check.
A refusal holds nothing of the call. No id, name, value or typed text is newly written into a test name or an assertion message, so nothing a check asserts on leaves the repo boundary differently.

Shared modules included by several targets. A helper that one target includes but does not use must raise no new dead-code warning under the clippy leg, and every non-stand target that includes the module must still compile. Lint allows stay local to the item that needs them.

The duplication measure is the code audit's own tool and recipe: jscpd 5.4.0 run through mise with node 26.8.2, Rust format, default 50 min-tokens, .gitignore respected, over packages, apps, tests, examples and the WPT runner. It is summarised as pct to two places, duplicated and total lines, clones, the src / test / mixed split by a tests directory segment, and the top ten. The reading is stated before and after.

The target the reading moves against is the earlier audit reading (3.80 % or 3.81 %, as whole pct or as the test split's pairs and lines, which P4 settles). The growth to reverse is test-to-test clone pairs.
Test code only. No product source, engine, driver, test harness or stand changes. No new crate or dependency, and the workspace manifest and lockfile stay unchanged.
Stand checks run their scenarios in both layout modes. A shared boot or act helper must keep each check running in every layout mode it ran in before.
Where moved setup opens a telemetry capture, the capture still opens before the check's own recorder. The helper keeps that order.
The founder is away. A fork that needs his call is written to founder-forks.md in the run directory, and the least-change option stands meanwhile.

body: The restructure's invariant: the stand checks' boot of a stand task or fixture, their act through a driver session, and their read of an answer (refusal, diff, caused, snapshot text) move into shared helpers; every check keeps the same test functions under the same names, the same assertions on the same readings in the same layout modes, no assertion's subject or bound moved into a helper, no test weakened, skipped or ignored — held by the stand checks themselves running unchanged.

A refusal holds nothing of the call: a helper that reads a refusal answer, or builds a test name or assertion message from a diff, caused, snapshot-text or refusal reading, writes no id, name, value or typed text into it that was not there before.

Caller input is never echoed: shared helpers that act through a driver session (type, key, click with ids and text) pass the call content to the session only and print or format none of it into output a check leaves behind.

Masked control values stay masked in what a helper reads: snapshot text and session replies for password and file inputs carry the masked stand-in, and a helper reading them asserts on nothing past it.
One target a file: no test file merged, split or renamed, no test target added or removed; the blitz-tests target pin and the stand-repeat leg's named targets stay as they are.
No new crate or dependency, manifest and lockfile unchanged: the blitz-tests crate stays unpublished, its test harness takes no tracing and no style dependency, and builds stay locked.

A shared helper added to a module that non-stand targets also include keeps every including target compiling with no new dead-code warning under the clippy leg, by the module's existing dead-code allowance convention.

The measure the chunk is read by: the code audit's jscpd recipe (pinned node and jscpd version, rust format, default min-tokens, gitignore respected) summarized as pct to two places, duplicated and total lines, clones, the src/test/mixed split and the top ten — stated before and after against the readings 3.80, 3.81 and 3.89 percent and test pairs 266, 291, 307.

Helpers that boot a driver session take the session state directory as a parameter, keep it owner-only and within its path-length bound, and clean up only their own files non-recursively, as the moved setup did.

Helpers reading answers through the session socket keep to its closed request grammar (hello, call, stop) and its reply forms (accepted, refused, oversize, refused malformed or version) as the moved setup did, without new verbs or fields.

body: The restructure's invariant: the stand checks' boot of a stand task or fixture, act through a driver session and read of an answer (refusal, diff, caused, snapshot text) move from each stand check into shared helpers, and each check keeps the same test functions under the same names, the same assertions on the same readings in the same layout modes; the existing stand checks themselves, run in the fast test leg and the stand-repeat leg, hold it.

One test target per file stands: no blitz-tests test file merged, split or renamed, no test target added or removed, the blitz-tests manifest's targets and the stand-repeat leg's named targets unchanged.

Where a shared helper may live: under the blitz-tests shared test modules, which are no target; session-check helpers in the one module the session checks share, fixture helpers in the one shared fixtures module, stand tables in the one shared stand-tables module.
A helper moves setup and reading code only, never an assertion's subject or bound; no test is weakened, skipped or ignored, and no expected value moves out of the check that asserts it.

Nothing a check asserts on leaves the repo boundary differently: no id, name, value or typed text newly written into a test name or an assertion message; refusals hold nothing of the call, test failures print no argument value, call assertions carry a row index only, a typed password never leaves.
A shared helper that a non-stand target also includes keeps that target compiling with no new dead-code warning under the clippy leg over the workspace.

The duplication reading stated before and after by the code audit's own jscpd recipe and summary (pct to 2 places, duplicated and total lines, clones, the src / test / mixed split, the top ten), read against the audit's metric rows: 3.80, 3.81, 3.89 % with test pairs 266, 291, 307 and src pairs 217, 223, 223.
Stand checks run in both layout modes: a shared boot or act helper keeps each check exercised in every layout mode it ran in.
Stand checks run under the bundled pinned real font with no skip: a shared boot helper keeps the bundled font and adds no font-absent skip path.
Stand checks hold a zero-failure budget over three stand-repeat rounds: the folded checks still pass every round.
Stand timers and time in the folded checks stay driven by delivered ticks and virtual time through advance; a shared helper adds no sleep or wall-clock read.
Test code only: no product source, engine, driver, harness or stand change, no new crate or dependency, the workspace manifest and lockfile unchanged.

test data a helper builds is stated in code, nothing seeded, and fixture pages are stated once in the shared fixtures module
